title: Two Negative Catalysts in a Week, One Asset That Didn't Flinch
summary: On September 16, the FOMC raised the federal funds rate 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, its first increase since July 2023.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways:


-


FOMC hike was priced in, the dot plot wasn't. Sixteen of eighteen FOMC members now see at least one more hike this year, with the median rate path revised up at every horizon; this is the real signal for positioning, not the 25bp move itself.


-


Bitcoin's non-reaction is the story. While gold, equities, and the dollar all moved exactly as a hawkish surprise would predict, bitcoin dipped and fully round-tripped within hours, a materially different pattern than prior hiking cycles.


-


Two bad catalysts, one muted response. Bitcoin absorbed both the Fed's hawkish tilt and the Clarity Act's Senate failure in the same week without a sustained selloff, suggesting bad news (monetary and regulatory) is being priced in rather than driving fresh selling.


## The Fed Resumes Hiking - Gold and Equities Flinch, Bitcoin Shrugs


On September 16, the FOMC raised the federal funds rate 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, its first increase since July 2023. The vote was unanimous, 12-0, notable as a sign of committee support for a new chair's first hiking decision. The hike itself was no surprise, with odds already above 90% heading into the meeting. The real news was the tone and the dots that came with it.


The instinct is to treat "first hike after a long pause" as the opening move of a new tightening cycle, the way 2004 and 2015 both kicked off multi-year hiking paths. We'd resist that framing. Chair Warsh spent the press conference disclaiming forward guidance ("I'm not in the forward guidance business").Instead, Warsh walked through three specific catalysts that changed his mind over the intermeeting period; labor market strength, inflation trend data, and geopolitics. That explanation reinforces Warsh’s characterization of a committee reacting meeting by meeting, not one committing to a path.


However, the dot plot cuts against that framing, it tells a story of higher for longer. The median expectation moved up at every horizon from June to September, with 2026 now at 4.1% (from 3.8%) and 2027 also at 4.1% (from 3.6%). That means the committee no longer sees rates declining next year the way it did three months ago. Sixteen of eighteen participants see at least one more hike before year-end, which frames the move as a down payment rather than a one-and-done adjustment.


The direction of that revision, up rather than down, is what we believe matters here, independent of the exact terminal number. The dot plot alludes to a Fed that doesn’t think it's close to done.


## Everything Repriced as Expected, Except Bitcoin


The initial market reaction ran through the traditional playbook almost exactly as the textbook would predict, with one conspicuous exception. The dollar strengthened. Short-end Treasury yields jumped, with the 10-year topping 5% again. Equities sold off, with the S&P 500 down 1.4% in the wake of the announcement. Gold gave back its morning gains within roughly half an hour, with gold down about $100 on the day. All standard hawkish monetary policy moves.


Bitcoin didn't play its assigned role. It dipped toward $75,000 immediately after the announcement and recovered to the $76,000 to $76,700 range within hours, essentially round-tripping the news. That's a meaningfully different pattern than prior hiking episodes in this asset's history, where bitcoin has often traded as a high-beta risk asset and sold off in sympathy with, or ahead of, equities.


There's real information in that combination. In our view, bitcoin's resilience to the hike, paired with a similarly muted reaction to the Clarity Act's failure in the Senate last week, suggests that bad news, both monetary and regulatory, is already being absorbed into digital asset prices rather than driving fresh selling.


Our read is that bitcoin failing to sell off on two negative catalysts in the same week is a more meaningful signal than either data point on its own.
